title: Choose Hexacomb’s new visual world
question: Service Dispatch is the strongest fit: sleek, local, and built around one accountable technology partner. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Service Dispatch
options.lineage: Central Valley utility dispatch boards and work-order packets
options.thesis: One local desk receives every technology problem, routes it, and owns it through resolution.
options.viewport: A crisp dispatch board turns websites, software, AI, and IT into four routed work orders beside a direct local promise and one primary call action.
options.risk: Could feel municipal if Marco’s human presence and plain voice are too quiet.

options.label: Signal Bridge
options.lineage: analog VU-meter bridges in recording studios
options.thesis: Every business system stays visible, balanced, and out of the red.
options.case: Strong product clarity, but owners may read studio equipment before local business support.
options.viewport: A row of four instrument meters names the four services while the promise and call action sit on the mixing-desk label strip.
options.risk: The audio metaphor can narrow a broad technology offer.

options.label: Layered Service Map
options.lineage: folded and layered Łowicz paper-cut systems
options.thesis: Each service is a distinct layer that becomes one complete operating picture.
options.case: Memorable and human, but the craft language weakens dependable technical authority.
options.viewport: A precise layered roundel becomes a live service map around a plain-language offer and direct call action.
options.risk: It can drift toward festival branding instead of a serious operating partner.

options.label: Local Paste-up
options.lineage: photocopied punk zines and neighborhood handbills
options.thesis: Technology advice with the human fingerprints and directness of a local operator.
options.case: High local personality, but its deliberate disorder conflicts with calm dependability.
options.viewport: A paste-up front page leads with the real offer, Marco’s portrait, and torn service tickets pinned in reading order.
options.risk: The grit can look improvised where the business needs controlled confidence.

canonCard.label: The polished agency standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar premium service site with a clean hero, proof row, service blocks, process, and contact form.
canonCard.viewport: A strong two-column hero with a business photo, concise promise, dual calls to action, and compact trust proof.
canonCard.risk: Clear and credible, but easier to confuse with another modern web agency.
